youtube.title: Australia Sent the Army to Fight Birds. The Birds Won. | The Great Emu War
youtube.description:
In late 1932, about 20,000 emus were damaging wheat farms in Western Australia. The government sent soldiers of the Royal Australian Artillery under Major G.P.W. Meredith, armed with Lewis machine guns. The birds scattered, the guns jammed, and by Meredith's own account nearly 9,860 rounds were fired for a claimed 986 kills, a figure historians dispute. The army was withdrawn within weeks; farmers later turned to fences and bounties.

📂 Case File #021: The Great Emu War

Sources: Mental Floss, "When Australia Went to War With Its Emus"; TheCollector, "The Great Emu War".
